task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 1 of 3. Your first pass (commit b13a523) was FAILED at the step-02 REVIEWER gate. **The five rules themselves were all found TRUE, their evidence all verified against source, and the commit confirmed additive with zero deletions — b13a523 is NOT reverted and this rework is additive on top of it.** What failed is that two of the rules are not actually in force where they need to be, plus four smaller consistency defects. Read handoffs/ADHOC-20260821-002/step-02-reviewer-gate.json's result in full — it names each gap and the change that closes it.

Seven items. G1 is the blocker.

**G1 (BLOCKER) — R3 is precedence-inverted, so the rule you wrote is optional as shipped.** You made the mutant run mandatory in WF-03 (a workflow doc, rank 3 in core-directives' Instruction Precedence). But `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` line 28 (a ROLE file, rank 2 — HIGHER) still reads that the validator should 'confirm the spec states (and, if you can verify it yourself cheaply, confirms) that the test actually failed against the pre-fix code.' A validator applying the precedence chain CORRECTLY concludes the mutant run is discretionary. ORCH confirmed this text firsthand at that line. This is the worst possible shape for a weak-model pipeline: a new mandatory rule sitting underneath the permissive text it exists to tighten. Amend that role file's WF-03 clause so applying and running at least one reported mutant is mandatory — not subject to a cheapness test, and explicitly not satisfiable by reading the producer's reported counts.

**G2 (MAJOR) — R3 tells a gate agent to mutate `lib/` and never tells it to revert.** Gate steps are bound by 'no file outside handoffs/ is modified', so as written the rule instructs an agent to violate its own scope, and a weak model can leave a deliberately-broken module on the branch. The source run avoided this only because its handoff carried an explicit revert-and-verify acceptance criterion, which did not survive into the general rule. Add the technique actually used: a throwaway `git worktree`, or `git checkout -- <path>` followed by verifying `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` is empty AND the test file re-runs green. State that a mutant is a temporary probe and that leaving one behind is a defect.

**G3 (MAJOR) — `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md` is a required home, and the load-bearing rule there is R1, not R2.** REVIEWER's ruling, and it understates nothing: GIT_MERGE.md makes Step Final agents run the full suite in two places with no attribution rule available. Its Precondition (around line 26) requires the suite 'has been run and reported green in this run's own' work, and step 5d treats any post-rebase `mix test` FAIL as a BLOCKER routed to ISSUE-FIXER. Against a suite carrying a standing 13-15 pre-existing failures **both are literally unsatisfiable** — and the only way agents have been reconciling them is exactly the count-matching R1 now forbids. So R1 is unreachable at the one step where a wrong attribution reaches main. ORCH confirmed both passages firsthand. Add an attribution pointer at step 5d and at the Precondition, pointing to R1's canonical home rather than restating it, and make clear that 'green' means 'no failure attributable to this branch under R1', not 'zero failures'.

  For R2 in the same file: a POINTER ONLY, one line under step 2 (which already forbids `git add -A` for this same shared-checkout reason). Do NOT restate `git push origin <sha>:main` there — GIT_MERGE never pushes to main directly (it uses a feature branch and a PR), so the single-SHA push rule would risk being misapplied inside the PR flow.

**G4 (MINOR) — add a cross-reference between R1 and core-directives' Unblock-Everything.** They compose, and R1 supplies what that directive was missing: its 'Scope boundary' paragraph draws the blocking-versus-merely-noticed line but never says how to decide which side a test failure falls on. They sit about seventy lines apart in one file with no link.

**G5 (MINOR, and it matters more than its severity suggests) — WF-02 Step 4 item 3 tells TEST-RUNNER to FILE an uncovered failure.** ISSUE_QUEUE.md was amended earlier today so that only ORCH calls the queue and 'the discovering agent reports the finding'. As written, WF-02 instructs TEST-RUNNER to do what ISSUE_QUEUE forbids — and worse, filing by a non-ORCH agent is what reintroduces the id-collision class that this morning's queue change exists to prevent. Restore the deferring parenthetical that core-directives' version carries: the failure is called out and REPORTED to ORCH, which files it.

**G6 (MINOR) — give WF-04's version the same four-point checklist form as WF-02 Step 4.** It is currently prose of comparable length but harder to execute and harder to report against point-by-point.

**G7 (MINOR, but it is the exact hazard this gate was asked to catch) — R1 states its two structural tests as if exhaustive, and they are not.** The very run R1 is drawn from cleared its failures by a THIRD argument: a demonstrated non-branch mechanism — orphaned `erl.exe` processes holding ~160 leaked connections, and stale rows in a guard-backup table whose parent tenant no longer existed, neither of which is expressible as 'the failing file is not in the diff', and that is also the class where a merge-base re-run is least reliable because it reproduces intermittently. Read literally, an agent facing this suite's DOMINANT failure class satisfies neither named test, and the predictable response is to assert the git-diff test loosely — which is precisely the false-compliance failure mode this rule exists to prevent. Add a third route explicitly: a demonstrated non-branch mechanism, evidenced by a measurement of the actual mechanism rather than by assertion, with the orphaned-process and stale-row cases cited as the worked examples. Keep the requirement that anything still unattributed is reported and filed.

Do NOT revert or rewrite b13a523's content except where these seven items require it. Do NOT touch code, tests, `docs/issues/`, `docs/requirements.yaml`, `docs/status/`, or ORCH's `handoffs/registry.json` and `handoffs/orchestrator.log`. Another session may be active in this checkout — if a file changes under you between read and write, re-read and re-apply.
acceptance_criteria: G1 -- .claude/agents/test-design-validator.md's WF-03 clause makes applying and running at least one reported mutant MANDATORY, with the cheapness qualifier removed and reading the producer's counts explicitly named as insufficient. Quote the before and after text
G2 -- The mutation rule states the revert-and-verify technique concretely and says a left-behind mutant is a defect

G3 -- GIT_MERGE.md carries an R1 attribution pointer at BOTH step 5d and the Precondition, and 'green' is redefined as 'no failure attributable to this branch under R1' rather than 'zero failures'. R2 gets a one-line pointer under step 2 only, with no restatement of the single-SHA push command
G4 -- R1 and Unblock-Everything cross-reference each other
G5 -- WF-02 Step 4 item 3 no longer instructs TEST-RUNNER to file; it reports to ORCH, consistent with ISSUE_QUEUE.md
G6 -- WF-04's attribution guidance is in the same four-point checklist form as WF-02 Step 4
G7 -- R1's structural routes include the demonstrated-non-branch-mechanism route, with the orphaned-process and stale-row worked examples, and evidence-of-mechanism required rather than assertion
The five rules' existing text from b13a523 is preserved except where these items require amendment -- verify with git diff that nothing else was rewritten
Only the six files in owned_modules and your own handoff are modified

result.summary:
All seven items addressed, additively on top of b13a523. Six files changed, 135 insertions / 19 deletions. EVERY ONE of the 19 deleted lines is at a site an item explicitly required amending -- G1's cheapness clause (3 lines), G4's Scope-boundary sentence (1), G7's 'one of these two things' framing plus its route-2 terminator (3), G3's step-5d 'If FAIL:' line (1), G5's item-3 (2), G7's WF-02 item-1 (3), G6's WF-04 prose paragraph (6). No other line of b13a523's rule text was touched; verified with `git diff -U0 | grep '^-[^-]'` and reading each hit. `git status --porcelain` shows exactly the six owned_modules files plus this handoff -- nothing else.

G1 (BLOCKER) CLOSED. `.claude/agents/test-design-validator.md` BEFORE: 'For a WF-03 regression test specifically: confirm the spec states (and, if you can verify it yourself cheaply, confirms) that the test actually failed against the pre-fix code.' AFTER: the cheapness parenthetical is GONE ('confirm the spec states, and verify yourself'), followed by a new bolded clause: where the pre-fix failure is that the code did not exist, the validator 'MUST additionally apply at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutants to the shipped logic yourself, run the suite, and quote your own measured counts. This is mandatory -- it is not subject to a cheapness test, and it is not satisfied by reading TEST-DESIGNER's reported counts (that is copying a claim, not validating one).' The precedence inversion is resolved at rank 2: the role file is now at least as strict as WF-03, so a validator applying Instruction Precedence correctly now reaches MANDATORY from either direction.

G2 CLOSED. WF-03's mutation subsection now opens its new final block with 'A mutant is a TEMPORARY PROBE. Leaving one in the tree is a step failure', names the scope conflict it resolves ('a gate step is otherwise bound by no file outside handoffs/ is modified'), and gives two concrete techniques: preferred throwaway `git worktree`; or in-place with `git checkout -- <path>` and a VERIFIED revert -- `git status --porcelain lib/ test/` empty AND the test file re-runs green, both quoted in result.summary. The WF03-ISS0106-20260821 precedent is cited with the note that it held only because that run's handoff asked for it, 'stated here so it no longer depends on a per-run handoff remembering to ask'. The same two-technique rule is mirrored in the role file so it travels with G1's mandate.

G3 CLOSED, in the shape REVIEWER specified. (a) Step 5d: a warning block after `mix test` -- attribute each failure structurally per core-directives, 'Green at this step means NO FAILURE ATTRIBUTABLE TO THIS BRANCH, not zero failures', do not compare counts, structurally-cleared failures are filed/forwarded and do not block, unattributed blocks; the terminator is re-worded to 'If FAIL (i.e. at least one failure is attributable to this branch, or is unattributed)'. (b) Precondition: a 'What reported green means here' paragraph making the same redefinition, naming the standing 13-15 and stating that 'zero failures' would make the precondition unsatisfiable and is not what it means. Both point at R1's canonical home and explicitly do not restate it. (c) R2: ONE line under step 2 only, reusing that step's existing shared-checkout rationale -- 'stage by explicit filename only (already required above) and push only your own commits; see ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1'. `git push origin <sha>:main` is deliberately NOT restated, per the stated reason that GIT_MERGE never pushes to main directly.

G4 CLOSED, both directions. Unblock-Everything's Scope boundary now carries the inline clause 'for a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching below, not by judgement'; R1 opens with the reciprocal pointer naming Unblock-Everything's Scope boundary and which side each verdict lands on.

G5 CLOSED. WF-02 Step 4 item 3 now reads 'called out AS SUCH and REPORTED FOR FILING per ISSUE_QUEUE.md ... You report the finding; you do NOT call the queue or gh yourself. Only ORCH allocates issue ids (ISSUE_QUEUE.md, amended 2026-08-21)', with the id-collision rationale named so a future agent can tell why. Same wording applied to WF-04's item 3 for consistency.

G6 CLOSED. WF-04 Step 1's prose paragraph is now the same fenced four-point checklist as WF-02 Step 4, same four points in the same order, carrying G5's and G7's amendments.

G7 CLOSED. R1 now states THREE routes, not two: route 3 is 'a demonstrated mechanism outside this branch, stated causally, and evidenced by a MEASUREMENT of the actual mechanism, never by assertion that one probably exists.' A following block explains why it exists ('this suite's DOMINANT failure class, and it satisfies neither of the first two' -- route 1 has no failing file to check against the diff, route 2 is least reliable for intermittents) and gives both worked examples with what counted as evidence: orphaned erl.exe processes holding ~160 leaked connections to letflow_test (evidence: the enumerated processes and the measured connection count), and stale guard-backup rows whose parent tenant no longer existed (evidence: the queried rows and the demonstrated absent parent). It closes with the anti-false-compliance sentence REVIEWER asked for -- 'if you find yourself about to assert route 1 loosely because neither test quite fits, that is route 3 without its measurement, and it is not an attribution' -- and keeps the filing requirement: 'If you can show none of the three, you may not call the failure pre-existing -- report it as unattributed and file it.' The three-route form is propagated to both compressed checklists (WF-02 Step 4 item 1, WF-04 Step 1 item 1), each ending 'If you can show none of the three, the failure is UNATTRIBUTED -- report it as such, don't stretch (a) to fit.'

SCOPE. No code, tests, docs/issues/, docs/requirements.yaml or docs/status/ touched -- this is a pipeline-rules run, not a requirement, so no status flip or status-history append applies. I did not write handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH's). completed_at read from the clock via `date -u`, not from memory. Not pushed, per instruction.

issues.description: Carried forward from this handoff's own context block, not introduced by me: this rework is recorded as its own handoff file rather than by incrementing rework_count on step-01 and re-routing it, which is what ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5 prescribes. The reasoning (step-01 is COMPLETED with a full result block; editing it in place would overwrite the record of the first pass) is sound and matches the append-not-overwrite convention the rest of the doc set uses, but the divergence should be fixed AT THE SOURCE in ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5 rather than re-decided per run. Flagged per core-directives' 'Never resolve a conflict silently'.

G3's redefinition of 'green' is now stated in GIT_MERGE.md's Precondition and step 5d, but the PR body template at step 7 still prints the bare lines 'mix compile --warnings-as-errors: PASS' and 'mix test: PASS'. An agent that has correctly attributed a non-zero failure count will be writing 'PASS' next to a run that reported failures, with nothing on the PR recording the attribution. Suggested follow-up (not done here -- it changes an artefact template rather than a rule, and was not in any of the seven items): have the template carry the attribution verdict, e.g. 'mix test: PASS (N pre-existing failures, each structurally attributed -- see <handoff>)'.

The re-gate should check G1's fix specifically for PRECEDENCE consistency in both directions -- the rank-2 role file and the rank-3 workflow doc must now agree that the mutant run is mandatory -- and should confirm route 3 in R1 did not weaken routes 1 and 2.
